premise: At 57, after 28 years as a legal secretary, I cashed out my $139,000 401(k) to open a vintage typewriter restoration and custom typewriter-paper shop with my half-sister, notarizing a 50% stake and free typewriter maintenance for my church’s community newsletter; after a film-studio prop house offered $610,000 for the restored 1920s Corona and Remington machines and client list, she forged a dissolution, sold the inventory, and mailed me a $4,500 'platen' check. I found our original partnership agreement inside the hollow base of a 1920s Royal typewriter, voided the sale, and now run 'Carriage of Deceit Typewriters,' where she polishes key levers in a smock that says 'Shifted My Pension' and every repair ticket prints her fraud-docket number.
